chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Hamza ibn Humran, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the one who says, 'Free me, for You withheld me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is freed where he was withheld.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Or should he not say it?'
ai.seo_question: What is the correct supplication for a pilgrim prevented from completing Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the specific supplication for breaking the state of Ihram when prevented by an obstacle, confirming that the phrase 'Free me where You withheld me' effectively lifts the obligation in that specific context. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of *rukhsah* (dispensation), emphasizing that the divine law accommodates practical impediments without nullifying the core ritual status. The Imam’s concise affirmation highlights the precision required in ritual language to ensure the pilgrim’s intent aligns with the legal requirements for exiting Ihram.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Hamza Bin Humran who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the one who is saying, ‘Free me whereas You<sup>azwj</sup> withheld me’ (the obligations of Hajj). He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Freed him where he was withheld’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Or should he not say it’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Hamzah ibn Humran who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who says, ‘Release me as You have withheld me.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He has released him as He had withheld him.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Should he not say it?”
